title: Angle Trisection OQ02-OQ03 Extension: Gauss-Wantzel Arithmetic Bridge
description: Bridges Gauss-Wantzel axiom to Mathlib cyclotomic infrastructure. Proves arithmetic lemmas connecting φ(n) = 2^k to φ(n)/2 = 2^{k-1}, complete constructibility classification for n ∈ [3,50], and structural characterization via prime factorization. 55 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius OQ02-OQ03-Ext
meta.assumptions: None. All 55 theorems proved. Classification by native_decide and decide.

overview.historicalContext: Gauss announced in 1796 (at age 18) that the regular 17-gon is constructible with compass and straightedge, proving it in his 1801 Disquisitiones Arithmeticae. He identified the criterion: the n-gon is constructible iff n = 2^a × (distinct Fermat primes), where Fermat primes are primes of the form 2^{2^j}+1. Pierre Wantzel (1837) proved the converse (necessity), completing the characterization now called the Gauss-Wantzel theorem. The algebraic proof proceeds through three equivalences: (1) n-gon constructible iff [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] is a power of 2 (constructibility criterion); (2) [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2 (real subfield degree); (3) φ(n)/2 = 2^k iff φ(n) = 2^{k+1} (arithmetic step — proved here using Nat.totient_even). The arithmetic bridge in step (3) requires that φ(n) is always even for n ≥ 3, since -1 ∈ (ℤ/nℤ)* has order 2. Only 5 Fermat primes are known (3, 5, 17, 257, 65537); whether infinitely many exist remains open.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) φ(n) is a power of 2 iff φ(n)/2 is a power of 2 (for n ≥ 3). (2) A regular n-gon is constructible iff φ(n) is a power of 2. (3) Complete classification for n ∈ [3,50]: 17 constructible values (3,4,5,6,8,10,12,15,16,17,20,24,30,32,34,40,48).
overview.proofStrategy: Section I: arithmetic of powers of 2 (pow2_of_half_pow2, totient_pow2_iff_half_pow2). Section II: non-constructibility via odd prime divisors (not_totient_pow2_of_odd_prime_dvd). Sections III-VI: batch verification via decide/native_decide for all n ∈ [3,50]. Section VII: summary with explicit constructible list.
keyInsights: **Arithmetic bridge**: φ(n) even for n≥3 (since -1 ∈ (ℤ/nℤ)* has order 2). So φ(n) = 2^k iff φ(n)/2 = 2^{k-1}. This connects the maximal real subfield degree to the cyclotomic degree.
**Non-constructibility criterion**: If p | φ(n) for an odd prime p ≥ 3, then φ(n) is NOT a power of 2 — n-gon is not constructible. This handles all non-Fermat cases.
**Complete n ∈ [3,50] table**: 17 constructible n-gons: n = 2^a × (distinct Fermat primes). The remaining 31 values all have odd prime divisors in φ(n).

**Fermat primes in range**: Only 3, 5, 17 appear as relevant Fermat primes for n ≤ 50. Distinct-odd-Fermat-prime products in range: just 3×5=15 (since 3×17=51, 5×17=85, 3×5×17=255 all exceed 50). The remaining constructible n combine these with 2^a multipliers — e.g. 34=2×17, 30=2×3×5, 20=4×5, 24=8×3 — and pure powers of 2 (4, 8, 16, 32).

**Five-step proof decomposition**: Gauss-Wantzel splits into steps (a) [ℚ(ζₙ):ℚ] = φ(n) [Mathlib: IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank]; (b) cos(2π/n) generates ℚ(ζₙ)⁺ [geometric]; (c) [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2; (d) constructible ↔ power-of-2 degree [OQ02]; (e) φ(n)/2 = 2^k ↔ φ(n) = 2^{k+1} [THIS FILE]. Step (e) is the only purely arithmetic step — once (a)-(d) are assembled in Mathlib, step (e) is already done.

sections.title: Section I: Arithmetic Bridge — φ(n)/2 = 2^(k−1) iff φ(n) = 2^k
sections.summary: pow2_of_half_pow2: 2|m and m/2=2^k ⟹ m=2^{k+1}. half_pow2_of_pow2. even_of_pow2_ge_two. totient_even_of_ge_three: 2|φ(n) for n≥3. totient_pow2_iff_half_pow2: the key arithmetic bridge iff theorem.

sections.title: Section II: Non-Constructibility Criterion and Applications
sections.summary: TotientIsPow2 predicate. not_totient_pow2_of_odd_prime_dvd: general criterion. Applied to n=19,22,23,26,27,28,29 with explicit odd prime witnesses. Template: `not_totient_pow2_of_odd_prime_dvd (by decide) (by decide) (show q ∣ φ(n) by decide)`.
sections.mathContext: If odd prime $q \mid \varphi(n)$, then $\varphi(n) \neq 2^k$. Proof: $q \mid 2^k$ $\Rightarrow$ $q \mid 2$ (Nat.Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow) $\Rightarrow$ $q = 2$, contradiction.

sections.title: Sections IV–V: Totient Multiplicativity and Fermat Prime Characterization
sections.summary: totient_multiplicative: wraps Nat.totient_mul. totient_pow2_mul: TotientIsPow2 preserved under coprime products (φ(mn) = φ(m)φ(n) = 2^a·2^b = 2^{a+b}). not_totient_pow2_factor: contrapositive. totient_pow2_prime_iff: TotientIsPow2 p ↔ p-1 = 2^k (Fermat prime criterion).
sections.mathContext: $\varphi$ multiplicative: $\gcd(m,n)=1 \Rightarrow \varphi(mn) = \varphi(m)\varphi(n)$. Powers of 2 closed: $2^a \cdot 2^b = 2^{a+b}$. Fermat prime: $p$ prime with $p-1 = 2^k$.

sections.title: Section VI: Complete n ∈ [16,50] Classification
sections.summary: Constructible n ∈ [16,50]: 16,17,20,24,30,32,34,40,48 (TotientIsPow2 with witnesses k=3 or k=4). Non-constructible: 31,33,36,37,38,39,41,42,43,44,45,46,47,49,50 each with odd prime witness.

sections.title: Section VII: constructible_up_to_50 — All 17 Constructible n-gons
sections.summary: constructible_up_to_50: 17-component conjunction TotientIsPow2 n for each constructible n in [3,50]. Proved by refine with explicit exponent witnesses via decide.

conclusion.summary: Gauss-Wantzel arithmetic bridge fully formalized: 55 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. The arithmetic gap between cyclotomic field degree and real subfield degree is closed, with complete n ∈ [3,50] classification.
conclusion.implications: This file provides the arithmetic infrastructure needed to bridge Mathlib's cyclotomic field machinery (IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank) to the Gauss-Wantzel constructibility criterion. Once the geometric steps (cos 2π/n generates the maximal real subfield) are formalized, the full theorem would follow.
openQuestions: Can the full Gauss-Wantzel theorem be proved without the axiom conic_constructible_iff_power_of_two?
Can the classification be extended to all n (not just n ≤ 50) using Mathlib's Fermat prime formalization?
Are there infinitely many Fermat primes? (Open problem — only 5 known: 3, 5, 17, 257, 65537)

crossReferences.description: Parent OQ02-OQ03 introduced the TotientIsPow2 predicate and initial classification; this extension completes the arithmetic bridge and the full n ∈ [3,50] classification
OQ02 characterizes constructibility via field extension degree: n-gon constructible iff [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] is a power of 2; this file provides the arithmetic step connecting that degree to φ(n)

OQ03 proves the O(log d) halvings algorithm for checking constructibility; the TotientIsPow2 predicate proved here is what that algorithm decides, making the two files complementary (proof vs algorithm)

The root angle-trisection entry establishes the impossibility of trisecting a general 60° angle (3|φ(9)=6, so 9-gon is not constructible); the arithmetic machinery here applies directly to that impossibility argument
